headline: John Felton, chief financial officer of Amazon Web Services, said the boom in AI spending is sustainable, pointing to AI servers that pay back their cost in under three years.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a senior executive of the largest cloud firm speaks on the record, but the figures are the company's own claims.
importance_line: Investors and the many firms that rent AWS computing hear reassurance from the company that earns from AI demand, but the figures are AWS's own claims and local opposition to data centres is a risk the article notes.
summary: Axios reports, in an exclusive interview, that John Felton, chief financial officer of Amazon Web Services (Amazon's cloud-computing arm), says AI spending is sustainable, with AI servers paying back their cost in under three years and an order backlog of nearly $500 billion at the end of the second quarter. His comments follow a Gartner report, published on Wednesday 14 Oct, that more than $3.5 trillion of AI infrastructure spending "could be exposed to impairment" (could lose value) by the end of 2030, and Axios notes that AWS is among the companies best placed to withstand such risks.
notes: Read on Yahoo Finance, which carries Axios's own text; the original Axios link was not given, so the Yahoo page is the url. The interview date is not stated. The Gartner report is dated Wednesday 14 Oct 2026 by CFO Dive/Yahoo (C05-01); our 15 Oct edition carried a separate Gartner forecast about neocloud companies.
